Organizations today expect seamless scale, predictable latency and performance, and hyperscaler-like operational agility when building modern AI data centers. Achieving this level of excellence requires an end-to-end architecture where bandwidth, topology, software, optics, power, and cooling are tightly integrated and continuously validated for performance and reliability.


AI labs, Neoclouds, research institutions and enterprises face significant friction when deploying AI infrastructure at scale. High-bandwidth fabrics introduce complex congestion management challenges, vendor lock-in restricts flexibility, and validating fragmented hardware and software stacks consumes critical time and resources slowing deployment schedules for distributed, data-intensive workloads.


Celestica addresses these challenges by delivering high-capacity open hardware platforms, production-ready[SONiC®](http://sonicfoundation.dev/) Distribution software, and a set of comprehensive design, deployment, and post-implementation[Services](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/services-and-support) capabilities. By combining these offerings, Celestica enables organizations to confidently scale their AI network infrastructure with hyperscale efficiency.


## Open Hardware Designed for your AI Fabric


To achieve seamless scale and predictable latency, organizations need a hardware foundation free from vendor lock-in. Celestica reinforces this commitment through active contributions to the[Open Compute Project (OCP)](https://www.opencompute.org/contributions/?contributions&contributor=Celestica) , delivering open, standards-based platforms designed across multiple Ethernet generations. The Celestica network switch portfolio spans both sides of the AI data center: the[DS5001](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5001/) and[DS4150](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds4150/) for the AI front-end networks, and the[DS6001](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6001/) /[DS6000](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6000/) and[DS5000](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5000/) for AI back-end networks. Celestica also contributed the design of DS5000 2U 64-port 800GbE switch to OCP and is available on[the OCP web site.](https://www.opencompute.org/marketplace/it-infrastructure/celestica-ds5000-2u-64-port-800gbe-data-center-switch/)


By leveraging multi-rate breakout modes across both downlinks and uplinks, network architects can maximize logical switch radix, allowing a 1:1 non-blocking, 2-tier CLOS fabric to reach massive endpoint scale without the added latency and cost of a 3-tier network:


**DS6001/DS6000 (102.4 Tbps) based AI Back-End Fabric:**


- **800G Endpoints:** Utilizing 2×800G breakouts on all 64 physical ports expands logical DS6000 radix to 128 ports per switch (64 downlinks, 64 uplinks). An all-DS6000 2-tier fabric scales up to 8,192 non-blocking for 800G endpoints.
- **400G Endpoints:** Breaking out both downlinks and uplinks to 4×400G unlocks the full 256-port logical ports (128 downlinks, 128 uplinks). This yields a flat, non-blocking fabric scaling up to 32,768 non-blocking 400G endpoints again in a two-tier topology.


**DS5000 (51.2 Tbps) based AI Back-End Fabric:**


- **800G Endpoints:** Operating at native 800G (32 downlinks and 32 uplinks per leaf), a 2-tier fabric supports up to 2,048 non-blocking 800G endpoints.
- **400G Endpoints:** Breaking out both downlinks and uplinks to 2×400G doubles logical port density to 128 ports per switch (64 downlinks, 64 uplinks). This quadruples cluster capacity to support up to 8,192 non-blocking 400G endpoints.


**DS5001 and DS4150 based AI Front-End Fabric:**


- **Multi-Rate Flexibility:** DS5001 (25.6 Tbps) delivers 32x800GbE OSPF ports for leaf or spine roles, while the DS4150 (16 Tbps) is suitable for top of the rack with 24x400GbE downlinks and 8x800GbE uplinks. Together, these platforms give organizations the flexibility to migrate toward 800G at their own pace, with breakout support on the DS4150 and the DS5001 keeping existing 100G and 400G connections in service during the transition.
- **Multi-Tenant Isolation:** Deployments that need secure, multi-tenant front-end networks can use the DS5001 and DS4150. EVPN/VXLAN allows to create separate virtual network segments over the shared fabric, isolating each tenant’s traffic. The Broadcom Trident5 based DS4150 adds enhanced buffering, larger VXLAN table capacities, and a 100G SFP112 to support more tenant segments and 100G connections.


Ultimately, achieving hyperscale efficiency is not about forcing every network to the highest port speed overnight. It is about deploying an AI fabric with open switches that fits your specific scale, latency requirements, power and cooling envelope, and long-term migration path.


## SONiC Distribution by Celestica for AI and Data Center Deployments


The high-capacity Celestica hardware provides the physical foundation for seamless scale; it is the underlying software stack that dictates whether an architecture truly achieves hyperscaler-like operational agility. To overcome the friction of deploying complex proprietary, multi-tier topologies, organizations are constantly looking for an open, Ethernet-based operating system backed by rigorous performance testing and qualification.


[SONiC Distribution by Celestica](https://cls.celestica.com/software/celestica-sonic/) and our latest releases, solves the congestion and validation challenges inherent in data-intensive AI workloads. It transforms open hardware into production-ready AI fabrics by mapping advanced networking features directly to the operational needs of modern clusters:


- **Predictable AI Performance and Congestion Management:** To keep distributed workloads moving predictably and maximize XPU utilization, AI fabrics must minimize packet loss and manage congestion at sale. SONiC distribution by Celestica mitigates high-bandwidth congestion challenges with advanced controls for lossless fabrics, featuring Dynamic Load Balancing (DLB), User-Defined Field (UDF) / Queue Pair ID (QPID)-aware hashing, and Cut-Through Switching for lower latency. Furthermore, network operators can rely on features such as Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) and Prior-based Flow Control (PFC) to proactively manage traffic.
- **Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Advanced Routing:** SONiC Distribution by Celestica supports scale-out fabrics through BGP, Inter-VRF Dynamic Route Leaking, Attached-Host Routing (neighbor-to-/32 route injection), and VRRP Active-Active in MC-LAG. It also supports VXLAN overlays for multi-tenant designs to provide flexible fabric building blocks.
- **Programmable Observability and Hardened Security:** Operating like a hyperscaler requires programmable provisioning, telemetry, and strict security baselines to prevent disruptions. SONiC Distribution by Celestica equips operators visibility into hardware health through FEC error telemetry, Soft Error Rate (SER) statistics, Hardware Drop Counters, and Enhanced SerDes Diagnostics. It secures management access with REST Server Authentication and protects log transport with Syslog over TLS.
- **Seamless Platform Enablement:** Expanding an AI fabric shouldn't consume critical time and resources or require operational downtime. SONiC Distribution by Celestica enables administrators to seamlessly deploy across physical platforms and Virtual SONiC environments. Additionally, it streamlines Day 0 and Day 1 operations with features like Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP), DHCP Client on Front Panel Ports, VLAN Range Management, and a dedicated Factory Reset CLI, allowing operators to rapidly scale or repurpose switches without disrupting broader deployment schedules.


## Confidence Comes from the Complete System


The lesson from hyperscaler deployments is that building modern AI infrastructure is often not about deploying the fastest switch. True operational agility and predictable performance comes by treating the network as an integrated system, i.e., harmonizing high-capacity hardware, production-hardened software, optics, and power and cooling into a validated fabric.


Celestica brings this architectural mindset to organizations everywhere by unifying the three essential pillars of modern AI networking:


- **Open, High-Capacity Hardware:** Break free from vendor lock-in with open DS4150 and DS5001 switches for AI front-end networks and 1.6T DS6000 and DS6001 switches for the AI back-end networks. Build low-latency and multi-planar fabrics that scale horizontally across independent planes to connect to tens of thousands of endpoints, with fault isolation between planes.
- **Hardened Open Software:** Eliminate operational overhead through SONiC Distribution by Celestica, tailored specifically for data-intensive AI network fabrics.
- **Complete Validation:** Removing the guesswork and time drain of qualifying fragmented stacks exemplified with verified production deployments.


Backed by Celestica’s comprehensive design, deployment, and post-implementation services, you gain the scale and performance of a hyperscaler with the accountability of a single trusted engineering partner. Whether you are scaling an 800G cluster today or architecting a seamless migration to 1.6T, your infrastructure can achieve predictable latency, massive scale, and open flexibility out of the box.


Scaling modern AI workloads efficiently requires an architecture that seamlessly unified open flexibility with production-grade reliability. With Celestica’s validated high-capacity platforms, optimized SONiC software, and full-lifecycle deployment services, you gain architectural control alongside proven, predictable performance.
